parsed.study_design: Comparative qualitative case study of three groundwater basins using case material and administrative monitoring data
parsed.population_and_sample: Farmers, landowners, kareze shareholders, groundwater users, and governing institutions in the Kuchlak, Mastung, and Panjgur basins of Balochistan
parsed.exposure: Customary groundwater rights, local access regimes, the 1978 Groundwater Rights Administration Ordinance, permit rules, technology restrictions, and government subsidies
parsed.outcome: Groundwater exploitation for irrigated agriculture, aquifer depletion, declining water tables, collapse or preservation of karezes, and distribution of irrigation-water access
parsed.rationale: The paper empirically compares groundwater-management regimes in three Balochistan basins and examines legal and institutional rules, particularly in the “An Ordinance” and “Local Responses” sections (pp. 58–67). Its substantive service is groundwater extraction for irrigated agriculture, with outcomes centered on aquifer depletion and farmers’ irrigation access; the isolated drinking-water exception for Quetta on p. 60 is not analyzed as household water-service access. It therefore concerns water-resource and irrigation governance rather than household or community water or sanitation service access.
